title: Oxidation-Reduction Reactions
intro: **Oxidation** is loss of electrons. **Reduction** is gain. They always travel as a pair.

cards.title: 2.1.1 The Different Definitions of Oxidation and Reduction
body: The oxidation number is the electrical charge assigned to each atom in a given compound.
Even when atoms of an element are bonded together to form molecules, they have a zero oxidation number.

cards.title: 2.1.2 Determining Oxidation Numbers of Common Elements
body: Rule 2: The oxidation number of any simple metal ion or nonmetal ion is equal to the charge on the ion.
The oxidation number of hydrogen is +1 (citing rule 4).

cards.title: 2.1.3 Oxidizing and Reducing Agents
body: In general, chemical reactions can be grouped into two types based on the change of the oxidation numbers (the transfer of electrons).
Oxidation-reduction reactions (redox reactions), and non-oxidation reduction reactions (non-redox reactions).

cards.title: 2.2.1 What is Electrolysis?
body: Electrolysis is the process in which electrical energy is used to cause a non-spontaneous chemical reaction to occur.
An electrolytic cell is an apparatus for carrying out electrolysis.

cards.title: 2.2.2 The Mechanism of Electrolysis
body: The conduction of electricity through an electrolyte (either molten or aqueous state) is due to the migration of the ions towards their oppositely charged electrodes.
During the electrolysis, a battery or other DC sources move electrons through the wire to the electrodes.

cards.title: 2.2.3 Electrolysis of Molten Electrolytes
body: Lead bromide can be used to demonstrate the electrolysis of molten electrolytes because it has fairly lower melting point.
Decomposition of the electrolyte into its ions by heat.
